analysis.title: The Bank Of Nvidia Just Lost Its Chairman: Mapping Every Circular AI Deal That Now Hangs On Colette Kress
key_insights: Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang resigned effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and keeps the CFO job. NVDA fell more than 13% initially and closed about 4% lower. CoreWeave (CRWV) fell 11% the same day.

Nvidia's equity investment book was $99 billion as of July 26, about 13 times the year-earlier level. Recipients include AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Safe Superintelligence), neoclouds (CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN, Nscale), Meta, suppliers (Intel, Coherent, Lumentum, Marvell, Synopsys, Corning, Nokia) and IP deals (Groq, Poolside, Hugging Face).
The article describes the structure as circular. Nvidia buys a stake, the recipient commits to Nvidia hardware, and the cash returns as GPU orders.

Nvidia's 10-Q footnotes show $366 billion of future commitments, $56 billion of additional commitments and $108.5 billion of guarantees. These total $530.5 billion before the $99 billion equity book, post-July deals and the proposed $125 billion backstop of the $500 billion financing platform.

Supply and capacity purchase commitments rose to $279 billion from $119 billion three months earlier. Per the WSJ, Huang described the wafer and memory commitments as an avalanche while large cloud providers moved toward alternative chips.

The OpenAI Ohio backstop was cut in half under Kress's rework and capped at $105 billion in the final 8-K. Nvidia's CFO commentary says each generation deployed at the site could mean about 1.5 million GPUs and $150-200 billion of Nvidia revenue.

Goldman's James Schneider kept Buy and cut the target to $220 from $300. He expects Nvidia to honor announced commitments, but says new multi-party ecosystem investments at the same scale will be harder without Huang's convening power.

UBS's Tim Arcuri expects a pause in Nvidia's willingness and ability to do financing deals. A pause could pull about $50 billion or more out of the AI ecosystem, set against Nvidia free cash flow of about $50-60 billion a quarter.

William Blair downgraded NVDA to Market Perform. It says existing contracts survive but the next round of deals is at risk, and that Nvidia could face more competition from Broadcom and AMD, both rated Outperform.

Per Bloomberg, Nvidia's $500 billion AI financing platform with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman and KKR has produced no deals in three months. Nvidia offers residual value support on up to 25% of a deal and some partners want more. The earliest platform deal is January.

Broadcom backstopped $30 billion of a $35 billion Anthropic TPU debt deal in May and is backstopping about 72.5%, or $43 billion, of a second $63 billion Anthropic deal. This is a competing financing offer to Nvidia's 25%.

Raymond James's Sunaina Sinha Haldea expects lenders to want more compensation for uncertainty and scrutiny to spread across AI infrastructure deal markets. Saxo's Charu Chanana says it is not a financing crisis yet but could catalyze a broader repricing of risk in the AI ecosystem.

Neocloud debt depends on Nvidia guarantees. Nscale got $860 million of rent guarantees for Texas and is negotiating more than $5 billion of Nvidia credit support for West Virginia. CoreWeave euro bonds trade around 80 cents and Firmus pulled its IPO in October.

Per the WSJ, Nvidia paused some revenue-share credit support deals in late August and began turning off the tap in October. Kress had questioned how guarantees are valued and halved the OpenAI backstop. Huang's son-in-law ran some of the financing deals.
Nvidia reports Q3 on Tuesday Nov 17. The article says Kress's answer on the $500 billion platform will show whether Nvidia is still writing new financing or only servicing existing commitments.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman's James Schneider cut the target to $220 from $300 and kept Buy. Existing commitments will be honored, but new large ecosystem investments get harder without Huang.
William Blair's Sebastien Naji downgraded after Huang's exit. The risk is the next round of deals and Nvidia's ability to defend share into 2027.
William Blair names Broadcom as a vendor that could take share from Nvidia. AVGO was quoted at $353.80 and rated Outperform.
William Blair names AMD as a competitor that could gain from Nvidia's leadership disruption. AMD was quoted at $575.38 and rated Outperform.
CoreWeave fell 11% on the day it marketed a $4BN+ investment-grade loan where Nvidia is presumably the guarantor. A reprice of Nvidia guarantees hits the weakest, most indebted borrowers first.

sector_views.rationale: Neoclouds depend on Nvidia financing and guarantees. A pause or repricing of the backstop raises their cost of debt, and the bear case puts utilization in a 75-85% gray zone that does not repay debt before hardware is obsolete.
Lenders are expected to ask harder questions about who carries the risk and to demand more spread. CCC spreads are already near cycle wides.

earnings_insights: Nvidia reports Q3 on Tuesday Nov 17 under interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress. The $500 billion financing platform is expected to be a question on the call.
Nvidia's free cash flow is stated at $50-60 billion a quarter (UBS estimate and the article's own figure). UBS says a financing pause could remove about $50 billion or more from the AI ecosystem.
Nvidia's average monthly P/E fell from 23 in May to 16 in October per the WSJ. The company responded with what the article calls the largest buyback in history.
The 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26 shows supply and capacity purchase commitments of $279 billion, up from $119 billion three months earlier.
risk_factors: Nvidia pauses or shrinks new guarantees and equity investments under interim leadership, board scrutiny and a first-ever board chair.
Lenders reprice or reject Nvidia guarantees, raising borrowing costs for neoclouds and labs that depend on them.
The $500 billion financing platform stays at preliminary memorandums of understanding and produces no deals past January.
Customers shift to Broadcom, AMD or Google chips, since Broadcom offers larger backstops than Nvidia's 25%.
Nvidia's $279 billion of supply and capacity purchase commitments become a burden if GPU demand weakens.
Legal and regulatory scrutiny from the DOJ and House committees, plus uncertainty over a permanent CEO.
charts_described: Goldman's Top of Mind diagram of CoreWeave delayed-draw term loans shows the customer's credit rating in step two deciding how much debt the SPV can carry and at what price.
vol_and_positioning: NVDA initially fell more than 13% on the CEO resignation news and closed about 4% lower, which the article reads as concern about out-year earnings rather than the next quarter.
CCC credit spreads are described as already near cycle wides, which raises refinancing risk for neoclouds that lose Nvidia credit support.
The article says the market had already priced a wide Nvidia discount to the market because of concern that AI infrastructure growth slows without Nvidia's financing.
geopolitical: The DOJ is looking at customers' shipments of Nvidia chips and House committee chairs want a closed-door briefing on Nvidia.
cross_bank_references: UBS's Tim Arcuri lists financing as the first of three key areas of impact, consistent with Goldman's view that new deals get harder.
Goldman and William Blair both say existing contracts survive and the next round of deals is at risk.
Broadcom offers much more backstop than Nvidia per Bloomberg, cited as the reason partners pushed Nvidia to go above 25%.

tension_points.bull_case: The 2027 order book is signed, Nvidia trades at a trough multiple (P/E 16 in October), and Goldman expects every announced commitment to be honored.
tension_points.bear_case: The order book was filled largely by customers Nvidia financed or backstopped, so earnings and financing are the same question. Without Huang, new guarantees get smaller, slower and costlier, and UBS sees a pause that could remove about $50 billion from the ecosystem.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Kress's answer on the $500 billion platform at the Q3 report on Tuesday Nov 17, or a first platform deal announced by January, would test the bear case.

tension_points.bull_case: Lenders underwrite the chips and customer contracts, so capital does not walk away. Raymond James expects the cost to rise, not the access to vanish.
tension_points.bear_case: Neocloud debt is investment grade only because of Nvidia's guarantee. If providers discount that guarantee, the neoclouds are at risk, and the Palihapitiya bear case needs no accident, only 75-85% utilization.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Capital providers saying the Nvidia guarantee is not worth what it was a week ago, per a Fortune source, would confirm the bear case.
